import pandas as pd

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length3_27/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length3_27/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length3_27/training_2.csv", index_col=0)

# Step 1: Join Source0 and Source1 on 'user_id'
# Source0 columns: ['user_id', 'movie_id', 'rating', 'timestamp']
# Source1 columns: ['user_id', 'gender', 'age', 'occupation', 'zip']
# We only need 'age' and 'occupation' from Source1 for the target schema
df_01 = pd.merge(source0, source1[['user_id', 'age', 'occupation']], on='user_id', how='inner')

# Step 2: Join the result with Source2 on 'movie_id'
# Source2 columns: ['movie_id', 'title', 'genres']
# We only need 'title' from Source2 for the target schema
df_final = pd.merge(df_01, source2[['movie_id', 'title']], on='movie_id', how='inner')

# Reorder columns to match target schema:
# ['title': string, 'user_id': float, 'movie_id': integer, 'rating': float, 'timestamp': float, 'age': float, 'occupation': float]
# Ensure correct dtypes:
df_final = df_final[['title', 'user_id', 'movie_id', 'rating', 'timestamp', 'age', 'occupation']]

# Convert dtypes as required
df_final['title'] = df_final['title'].astype(str)
df_final['user_id'] = df_final['user_id'].astype(float)
df_final['movie_id'] = df_final['movie_id'].astype(int)
df_final['rating'] = df_final['rating'].astype(float)
df_final['timestamp'] = df_final['timestamp'].astype(float)
df_final['age'] = df_final['age'].astype(float)
df_final['occupation'] = df_final['occupation'].astype(float)

# Save the final dataframe to the target path
df_final.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_27/target_multisource.csv", index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_27/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_27/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_27/training_2.csv", index_col=0)

# Join Source3_27_0 and Source3_27_1 on user_id (inner join)
joined_01 = pd.merge(source0, source1, on="user_id", how="inner")

# Join the above result with Source3_27_2 on movie_id (inner join)
joined_all = pd.merge(joined_01, source2, on="movie_id", how="inner")

# Group by the leftmost non-float columns in target schema that are unique identifiers:
# According to target schema and hints:
# title (string), user_id (float), movie_id (int)
# user_id is float in target but originally int in source, still used as group by because it is an identifier
# Aggregate rating, timestamp, age, occupation by average (float columns)
grouped = joined_all.groupby(
    ["title", "user_id", "movie_id"], as_index=False
).agg({
    "rating": "mean",
    "timestamp": "mean",
    "age": "mean",
    "occupation": "mean"
})

# Reorder columns to match target schema exactly
final_df = grouped[["title", "user_id", "movie_id", "rating", "timestamp", "age", "occupation"]]

# Write to output CSV
final_df.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_27/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
